title: The Last Letter Again
premise: Zephyrine Whitlock, the coroner of Hollowmere, autopsies a stranger wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, and the only witness to the death is a woman officially listed as dead for three years: Marisol Vane, Zephyrine's childhood friend and first love. Following Marisol's trail of coded letters, Zephyrine uncovers a scheme by the town's beloved patriarch to fake deaths and launder fortunes through the cemetery records she herself maintains. In the climax, Marisol lures the patriarch into confessing at the graveside he faked for himself, and Zephyrine must choose between destroying the evidence that would ruin Marisol's new identity or burning it to protect the truth. She chooses truth — but keeps one letter back, the last letter again, addressed to her.
about_author: Cyrus Ravensworth is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade recording births and deaths in towns too small for secrets. They write mysteries about paper trails, small communities, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A drowned stranger washes up in Zephyrine's own stolen coat, and among his effects is a letter signed by Marisol Vane — dead three years, mourned by Zephyrine personally. The emotional beat is grief cracked open by disbelief; Zephyrine realizes the body was dressed to send a message, and she was the intended recipient.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with an interlude from Marisol watching from afar. Digging into burial records, Zephyrine finds three 'deaths' with no bodies and matching signatures — all notarized by patriarch Ambrose Fell. The beat is dread compounding into resolve as loyalty to the town collides with loyalty to a ghost who may be alive.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Was Buried
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals herself, explaining she faked her death to escape Fell's scheme and has been leaving letters as breadcrumbs, trusting only Zephyrine. But Fell knows she's alive, and the drowned man was his warning. The beat is reunion laced with terror — love rekindled under a countdown, as Fell moves to bury Marisol for real.

chapters.title: What the Ground Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging at Hollowmere cemetery. Zephyrine baits Fell into confessing over his own empty grave while Marisol records every word; when he turns violent, the town's found family — gravediggers, clerks, the widow he ruined — arrive as witnesses. The beat is catharsis: duty and truth finally aligned, sealed by the one letter Zephyrine keeps.
